card: Band phases: A phase 2Ch, B phase 10h, zombie phases 2000h/3400h (added to AX); explore separations that minimize A/B/zombie lane overlap.

analysis.latticeClass: All rev0 phases (A 2Ch, B 10h, zombies 20h/34h) are multiples of 4 pages and every band (0,3C,78,B4,F0) is too, so A, B and both zombie streams share one 400h lattice (arena 52h mod 400h). Steps 4400h (17 lattice points) and 2C00h (11 points) are coprime with 64, so every stream visits all 64 points. A page-phase change that is not a multiple of 4 moves the whole lattice by 100h/200h/300h (no in-page change, so the A4-at-addr=2-mod-4 parity is kept).
analysis.overlapInvariance: Lane overlap cannot be reduced by lattice separation: a 400h trail always covers exactly 1 point of any other 400h lattice per generation and an 800h trail exactly 2, whatever the offset. On a shared lattice the covered point is a shared anchor point, which is already the minimum. Phase choice only changes timing.
analysis.zombieLanes: Captured zombies quantize B's code address (get_ip in B), so their streams start at band_B+20h/+34h, 4 and 9 lattice points above B. They run at speed 2 and step 2C00h like B, so they lap B. Collisions are then set by phase drift, not by the starting offset.
analysis.partnerModel: agent2/night/scratch/A009/psim.mjs (A005 model with PA/PB parameters). Scanned all 64 A-B page deltas in steps of 4 pages. A was killed by B in 7-15 of 25 band combos at every delta, never earlier than round 1791. B was never killed. No delta removes partner kills.

candidates.label: s100
candidates.change: All streams moved down 100h: A add ah,2Ch->2Bh; B add ah,10h->0Fh; zombie BP 3400h->3300h, 2000h->1F00h (lattice 52h->352h mod 400h). Only 4 bytes differ from rev0.
candidates.notes: Strong: 1 win, 6 losses. lead_zrl03 +0.289, lead_zchain4 -0.200, LowKey -0.217.

candidates.label: s200
candidates.change: All streams moved down 200h: A 2Ah, B 0Eh, zombies 3200h/1E00h (lattice 252h mod 400h).

candidates.label: s300
candidates.change: All streams moved down 300h (= 100h up): A 29h, B 0Dh, zombies 3100h/1D00h (lattice 152h mod 400h).

candidates.label: s400 (control: same lattice class)
candidates.change: All streams moved down 400h: A 28h, B 0Ch, zombies 3000h/1C00h. Lattice stays at 52h mod 400h, so relative A/B/zombie offsets are unchanged. Only the start positions relative to the own band and own code move.
candidates.notes: ALL is above +0.006, but multi is -0.036: both cohorts lost (smulti-V6x3 -0.028, smulti-mix -0.044), which fails the coordinator's multi >= -0.02 gate. A pure translation is expected to be neutral by mechanism, so this is most likely noise. Trajectory-changing edits show screen spread of about +/-0.02 (s100..s400: -0.002, -0.024, -0.017, +0.021). Not marked promising. Cheap to include as an extra arm if the coordinator wants a second look.

threatFindings.threat: Moving the lattice class (all streams shifted 100h/200h/300h; no in-page change) costs heavily against the strong 2024-final/Chimera field
threatFindings.evidence: Screens tn359, ehn6q, xzyuh: strong -0.139, -0.133, -0.163 (W/L 1/6, 1/6, 0/7), each CI below 0. Same-class control nofsj: strong +0.022 [-0.077,+0.122]. So this is the lattice class itself, not shared base-arm luck. The losses are also present in all-2024-final cohorts (sstrong-3: TOM_ATO, WHS_Lucas, TOM_R_JS; -0.11..-0.28).
threatFindings.impact: Keep A, B and zombie phases at multiples of 4 pages. Page-level lattice shifts do not give a usable undercut.

threatFindings.threat: A/B/zombie lane overlap can be reduced by separating lanes (phase offsets)
threatFindings.evidence: Analytical: per-generation coverage of another stream's lattice is invariant (400h trail covers 1 point, 800h covers 2), and the shared lattice already makes collisions happen only at shared points. Model psim.mjs: no A-B page delta (64 tested) removes partner kills (7-15 of 25 combos at each). The off-lattice screens were not better.
threatFindings.impact: No phase-based fix for partner/zombie crossfire. The upper bound of the gain stays at about 0.004 (A005).

threatFindings.threat: B's first 600h trail ([band+10h,+16h)) and the zombie first trails ([+20h,+26h), [+34h,+3Ah)) overwrite B's own code, i.e. the zombie_entry and worker template that captured zombies still need
threatFindings.evidence: Static only. Each first trail overlaps B's code in about 11% of loads ((600h+CAh)/3C00h). But the 2025 zom20a-d jump to zombie_entry around rounds 15-30, before B's trail starts (about turn 60). Only late captures could be hurt: opponents' V6-family hooks via the shared [4A17h], or m050-lineage hooks via [5D13h]. Not isolated: s400 changes this overlap and also re-randomizes trajectories.
threatFindings.impact: Probably small. A test would need a trace job on zombie deaths after round 60.

threatFindings.threat: A 400h translation of all start positions (same lattice) changes the score
threatFindings.evidence: Screen nofsj ALL +0.0206 [-0.008,+0.049]; multi -0.036 in 2 cohorts. No mechanism found beyond the hypothesis above.

recommendation: Do not promote any A009 candidate. Rule out page-class lattice shifts: all three lose about 0.13-0.16 on the strong group. s400 (pure same-lattice translation) screened ALL +0.021 but fails the multi gate (-0.036) and has no mechanism, so it is most likely noise. At most, add it as a cheap extra arm in a confirmation run. Keep A 2Ch / B 10h / zombies 2000h/3400h. Partner and zombie lane overlap cannot be fixed by phase choice.
